Pomegranate Honey Fruit Salad

Served at: Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)

Serves 6Prep 15 min

Pomegranates are a traditional symbol of Rosh Hashanah, representing abundance and the hope for a year filled with good deeds. This refreshing fruit salad combines pomegranate seeds with other sweet fruits and honey, making it a festive and meaningful dish for the Jewish New Year celebration.

Ingredients

  • 2 large pomegranates, seeds removed (about 2 cups/300 g)
  • 2 medium apples, diced
  • 1 cup (150 g) seedless grapes, halved
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • Fresh mint leaves for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Carefully remove the seeds from the pomegranates and place them in a large mixing bowl.
  2. Add the diced apples and halved grapes to the bowl with the pomegranate seeds.
  3. In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, lemon juice, and ground cinnamon until well combined.
  4. Pour the honey dressing over the fruit and gently toss to coat all the pieces evenly.
  5. Transfer the fruit salad to a serving bowl and garnish with fresh mint leaves if desired.
  6. Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 2 hours before serving to allow flavors to meld.

Tips

  • Use a mix of red and green apples for added color and flavor.
  • To easily remove pomegranate seeds, score the fruit and break it apart over a bowl of water; the seeds will sink and the pith will float.
  • Add chopped nuts like walnuts or almonds for extra texture and a traditional touch.
